subject: Mutual action plan and billing buffers for evaluation (MAP: burst/overage clarification)
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-retail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + question on burst/overage buffers

Hi Neha / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising. Were moving to a short evaluation pilot and the procurement team asked for a mutual action plan (MAP) that ties milestones to pricing/commits. I attached a one-page MAP draft (Acme_MAP_v1.pdf).

Two quick clarifying items they want spelled out:
- During the 90-day eval ramp, what happens if we exceed our committed usage in a given week? Is there a burst/overage rate or a short-term buffer you can offer while we stabilize?
- Can we get the rate card broken down by token band (0-5M, 5-20M, >20M) for both committed and burst consumption?

Jordan will loop in procurement if this looks reasonable. Our objective is to avoid surprise invoices while giving the team room to ramp.

Appreciate a short note back with suggested guardrails so procurement can draft the SOW.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Retail

Attachment: Acme_MAP_v1.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + question on burst/overage buffers

Hi Maria — great to hear. Appreciate the MAP doc. High level answer: we can provide a short-term buffer during the evaluation ramp, plus explicit per-minute and daily caps to prevent runaway spend. Proposed approach (summary):

- Ramp buffer: 15% free burst allowance on top of the weekly committed baseline for the first 60 days of evaluation. This is to absorb onboarding spikes and prompt tuning.
- Overage pricing: burst beyond the buffer billed at a pre-agreed premium (1.6x committed per-token rate) until the customer either expands commit or rolls back to baseline.
- Per-minute and daily caps: we set a conservative per-minute QPS cap (configurable) and a daily hard cap that will prevent more than X tokens/day unless explicitly authorized.
- Rate card: I attached a simplified workbook (redwood-ratecard-2025.xlsx) with the committed vs burst bands and examples.

Next steps: if that buffer/premium looks ok, we can incorporate the numbers into the MAP and Marissa (CS) will add an onboarding checklist tied to the milestones. If procurement needs a finance-approved exception (discount or different premium), I can loop in Rishi for approval.

Proposed milestone cadence for the MAP:
1) Week 0: SOW signed and GTM kickoff (0.5 commit)
2) Week 2: Integration complete + 1st production test (metrics: 99th p95 < 500ms)
3) Week 4: 50% traffic route with monitoring and cost dashboard
4) Week 8: Full traffic + commit finalized (final commit starts)

I'll paste a one-paragraph summary you can attach to the procurement SOW if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-2025.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acme-retail.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + question on burst/overage buffers

Thanks — adding a few technical clarifications so expectations align during the ramp:

- Typical onboarding spikes weve seen are concentrated in short windows (10-30 minutes) as batch jobs or internal tooling execute. The 15% weekly buffer helps but its the per-minute QPS cap that prevents very large single-window cost events.
- We recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for Acme's reranking workflows; it reduces token volume by ~20-30% in our benchmarks and lowers burst exposure.
- If you expect scheduled batch runs (e.g., nightly re-indexing), mark those in the MAP as exempt from the buffer or run them under a separate commit to avoid unexpected overage calculations.

I attached a short example calc in the ratecard workbook showing scenario A (steady ramp) vs B (scheduled batch spike). Happy to hop on a 20-min session with your infra owner to map expected QPS to cap levels.

-Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in finance/renewals for visibility. Neha — provisional approval for a one-time evaluation concession: we can make the 15% ramp buffer non-billable for the first 60 days and cap the burst premium at 1.5x committed rate (instead of 1.6x) provided Acme commits to a minimum 6-month reserved baseline if they convert to Dedicated.

Conditions:
- This concession applies only during the 60-day evaluation window and is conditional on: signed MAP, SOW referencing the buffer, and a named infra owner from Acme for the QPS cap configuration.
- Finance will require the redwood-ratecard-2025.xlsx to be attached to the SOW and a short billing exception form (Ill send).

Neha — please confirm and get a signed MAP. Marissa, can you add the onboarding playbook for the 60-day period and a checklist for prefix caching?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
